The upper triangle is ABC, and the lower triangle is ABD. The angles marked in the figure are: at the upper vertex C is 60°, at B in the upper triangle is 61°; at A in the lower triangle is 60°, and at the lower vertex D is 59°. The five line segments are AC, CB, AB, AD, DB. Reasoning: In triangle ABC, ∠C=60°, ∠B=61°, so ∠A=180°-60°-61°=59°. In a triangle, a larger angle faces a larger side, so AC faces 61°, AB faces 60°, and BC faces 59°, so AC > AB > BC. In triangle ABD, ∠A=60°, ∠D=59°, so ∠B=180°-60°-59°=61°. Therefore AD faces 61°, DB faces 60°, and AB faces 59°, so AD > DB > AB. Now it is only necessary to compare the two possibly longest sides AC and AD. Use the sine theorem and use the common side AB: in ABC, AC/AB = sin61°/sin60°; in ABD, AD/AB = sin61°/sin59°. Because sin59° < sin60°, sin61°/sin59° > sin61°/sin60°, that is, AD > AC. Combined with the previous local ordering, AD is the longest of the five line segments.

在三角形 ABD 中，∠A=60°，∠D=59°，所以 ∠B=180°-60°-59°=61°。因此 AD 对 61°，DB 对 60°，AB 对 59°，所以 AD > DB > AB。
